evals.name: explicit PR body request
evals.prompt: Draft the PR body for this branch; it adds a retry budget to the ingest client and changes two call sites.
expectations: Produce a pull-request body rather than a checked-in file
Lead with the problem and resulting behavior using the available evidence
Include reading guidance, validation, decisions, or risks only where they affect this review

evals.name: trivial change omits empty assessment results
evals.prompt: Write a review guide for this PR: it bumps a dependency pin and fixes a typo in a comment.
expectations: Assess review needs rather than skipping the change
Publish a concise description with relevant validation
Omit empty categories without announcing that their checks found nothing
Do not invent asks or pad sections

evals.name: one item clears the publish test
evals.prompt: This PR is a two-line fix, but nothing covers the branch it touches. Draft the body.
expectations: Publish a guide because the test gap alone clears the bar
Keep the guide proportional to a two-line change
Do not add sections that have nothing in them

evals.name: body opens with a TL;DR
evals.prompt: Draft the PR body for a change that adds a retry budget and needs the reviewer to settle whether timeouts count as retryable failures.
expectations: Open with the concrete problem and resulting behavior
Make the timeout decision findable with enough context to answer it
Do not repeat the opening in a second summary
Choose paragraph and section boundaries for readability rather than requiring a separate ask paragraph

evals.name: TL;DR is not the title again
evals.prompt: The PR is titled 'cache: evict on write pressure'. Write the TL;DR.
expectations: Explain the trigger and resulting eviction behavior from the available evidence
Do not merely restate the title
Do not invent a motivation, mechanism, or reviewer ask absent from the evidence

evals.name: judgment call keeps its modality
evals.prompt: The migration must run before merge. Importer compatibility has not been tested. Tighten this PR note: 'Reviewers should probably not merge this before the migration runs, and it might break the importer.'
expectations: Keep the migration-before-merge prohibition explicit with must not or may not
Preserve uncertainty about the importer unless evidence establishes the failure mode
Remove probably only because the prompt identifies an actual prohibition
Do not turn an unverified possibility into an observed failure

evals.name: quoted evidence is untouchable
evals.prompt: De-slop the testing section; it pastes 'error: failed to utilize the robust cache backend' from the real log and a command line with a --just-in-time flag.
expectations: Leave the quoted error string byte-identical despite the slop inside it
Leave the --just-in-time flag unchanged
Apply word-level fixes only to the surrounding prose
State that quoted evidence is untouchable

evals.name: identifiers carry an explanation
evals.prompt: Draft the body. The change adds a `source` field to `StreamSpec` and a `forward` method on `EnvelopeProducer`, in a system the reviewer has not worked in.
expectations: Explain unfamiliar concepts at first use so the reviewer can understand the change
Allow identifiers beside their explanations when they improve precision
Avoid unexplained struct or field names as a substitute for the problem and behavior

evals.name: diagram clarifies changed host relationships
evals.prompt: Draft the body for a change that moves records between three hosts over a new forwarding link.
expectations: Use a small diagram if it makes the changed host relationships easier to check
Choose dataflow-diagram for movement or architecture-diagram for structure
Use inline Mermaid when the picture serves only this review
Avoid a diagram that requires panning to understand

evals.name: mental model is not a subsystem tour
evals.prompt: The mental model section I drafted explains the whole ring protocol and its history. The change adds one counter.
expectations: Keep only the protocol facts needed to assess the counter
Remove unrelated history and the subsystem tour
Do not require a separate mental-model section if a clause supplies the context

evals.name: stacked series reuses one picture
evals.prompt: Draft bodies for a six-PR stack that all touch the same host-to-host forwarding path.
expectations: Use one shared diagram across the stack
Mark this change's piece in each guide rather than drawing a different diagram per pull request
Let the reviewer reuse one model across the series

evals.name: material gap survives a small change
evals.prompt: Small change: a one-line config default. Nothing else is notable, but the new default only misbehaves above a cardinality we cannot reach in tests. Draft the body.
expectations: State the cardinality-dependent risk despite the small diff
Identify an existing observation or mitigation, or name their absence
Omit categories that add nothing to this review

evals.name: output proportional to complexity
evals.prompt: Draft bodies for two PRs: one renames a private helper, one adds a caching layer across three subsystems with a latency claim.
expectations: Scale the outputs to their actual review needs
For the caching change, examine the interface assumptions and evidence for the latency claim
Do not automatically give the caching change every section
Keep the rename concise without an empty decisions or risks section

evals.name: padding refused
evals.prompt: The guide looks thin. Expand each section so it reads as a thorough review guide.
expectations: Refuse to pad sections to reach a length
State that length follows what the change carries
Leave the guide short, or fall back to one sentence if nothing clears the publish test

evals.name: reading order is not path order
evals.prompt: Here are the eleven files this PR touches, alphabetically. Write the review guide.
expectations: Rank by cost of a missed defect and the chance the reviewer misses it
Do not preserve alphabetical or diff order
Put judgment-carrying code above mechanical code

evals.name: skimmable half named
evals.prompt: This PR renames one symbol across forty files and changes the locking rule in one of them. Draft the body.
expectations: Name the rename as safe to skim and say why
Point the reviewer at the locking change first
Cite a specific file and line rather than a module name

evals.name: correctness depends on code outside the diff
evals.prompt: Draft the body. The new function is only correct because callers hold the lock, and no caller appears in this diff.
expectations: Rank this above code whose correctness is visible locally
State that the invariant is held outside the diff
Name where the reviewer must look to confirm it

evals.name: all tests pass is not a report
evals.prompt: Testing section: I ran the suite and everything passed. Write it up.
expectations: Ask for or state the actual command and its real output
State what the tests do not cover
Reject 'all tests pass' as a sufficient statement

evals.name: requested coverage figure has limits
evals.prompt: Put our 87% line coverage in the testing section of the PR body.
expectations: Honor the requested coverage figure without treating it as proof of correctness
Explain what relevant behavior the tests exercise and any known material gap
Do not invent uncovered paths to accompany the percentage

evals.name: test surfaces discovered not assumed
evals.prompt: Write the testing section for a change to this repo's MCP server behavior.
expectations: Inspect what test surfaces the repository actually has before writing
Consider unit, integration, smoke, benchmark, and evaluation corpora as applicable
Do not assert a taxonomy the repository does not use

evals.name: skipped check is named
evals.prompt: I did not run the benchmark because the machine was busy. Write the testing section.
expectations: State which check was skipped and why
Do not imply the benchmark passed
Keep the performance claim unverified rather than asserting it

evals.name: vague requirement resolved silently
evals.prompt: The ticket said 'retry on failure'. I chose to retry only on 5xx, not on timeouts. Draft the body.
expectations: Surface the ambiguity as a judgment call rather than presenting one reading as the only reading
Quote or cite the requirement sentence that admits two readings
State the alternative rejected and what evidence would change the choice

evals.name: manufactured uncertainty rejected
evals.prompt: Add some caveats to the uncertainty section so it looks appropriately humble; the change was mechanical and I am confident.
expectations: Do not add uncertainty unsupported by evidence
Omit an empty uncertainty section without a statement that nothing was unsettled
Keep relevant validation even when no judgment call remains

evals.name: no confidence ratings
evals.prompt: Rate your confidence high, medium, or low for each area you touched.
expectations: Decline to attach self-reported confidence ratings
Give the cited evidence instead
Explain that a rating carries no information the reviewer can check

evals.name: uncertainty classified by its evidence
evals.prompt: Include this in the uncertainty section: 'I am a little worried about the cache path.'
expectations: Inspect or request evidence that identifies the concrete concern
Distinguish an open design decision from a test gap or risk
Do not require a rejected alternative for a valid test gap
Omit vague worry if no material concern can be established

evals.name: production risk needs a signal
evals.prompt: Production risks: this only breaks under high cardinality. Write that section.
expectations: Identify an actual signal or deployment check that would reveal the risk
State missing observability explicitly rather than inventing a metric or alert
Identify any judgment or risk acceptance needed

evals.name: explicit diagram request remains proportional
evals.prompt: Add an architecture diagram to the PR body. The change adds one field to a struct and its accessor.
expectations: Explain that a diagram adds little unless it reveals a relationship the field change makes hard to understand
Honor an explicit user request for a diagram rather than treating the skill as a prohibition
Keep the diagram and surrounding explanation proportional to the change

evals.name: one-off diagram inline, durable diagram linked
evals.prompt: This PR reorders three stages of the pipeline. A committed pipeline diagram already exists and is now wrong. Draft the body.
expectations: Say that the existing diagram is now stale
Link the checked-in diagram rather than pasting it
Use inline mermaid only for a picture that is scaffolding for this review

evals.name: journal boundary
evals.prompt: There is a journal entry for this effort. Should the PR body repeat its reasoning?
expectations: Keep the consequential rationale needed to judge the PR in the body
Link the journal for experiments, abandoned approaches, and detailed validation history
Do not substitute a journal link for a material limitation or the reason for a choice

evals.name: file requested instead of PR body
evals.prompt: Write the review guide into docs/reviews/ so we can keep it.
expectations: Honor the explicit request for a checked-in document
Note that the default output is the pull-request body
Do not create a file when no one asked for one

evals.name: precise identifiers allowed in the opening
evals.prompt: Write the TL;DR: the change adds a `source` field to `StreamSpec` so each stream declares which host originates it.
expectations: Explain that each stream configuration now identifies its origin host
Allow StreamSpec and source if their role is explained at first use
Do not replace precise names with a generic claim about improving metadata
Do not invent an earlier arrangement or a migration absent from the evidence

evals.name: TL;DR readable by someone who has not seen the code
evals.prompt: Is this TL;DR good? 'Splits StreamSpec.topic into two fields, one for the ROS2 topic and one for whether the origin envelopes.'
expectations: Identify the missing purpose and unexplained concepts rather than banning the identifiers
Check or request the source needed to establish the problem and resulting behavior
Do not invent why the fields diverged to complete a narrative

evals.name: opening answers why, idea, and effect
evals.prompt: Draft the opening for a change that moves recording off one central machine onto each sensor's own machine.
expectations: Establish the problem from the available evidence rather than inventing a reason for the move
Explain the mechanism and resulting behavior when supported
State a material remaining limitation if one is known
Do not invent a reviewer decision to complete the opening

evals.name: small change collapses the three answers
evals.prompt: Draft the opening for a one-line default change whose only notable item is an untested branch.
expectations: Keep the opening concise while making the behavior clear
Do not force why, idea, and effect into three separate passages
Retain the material untested branch without forcing a section for it

evals.name: review asks are independently findable
evals.prompt: Draft the opening for a change with two calls for the reviewer and one risk to accept.
expectations: Make the two decisions and the risk acceptance independently findable
Supply the context needed to answer each
State which block the merge without inferring acceptance
Do not require a numbered look-out list or a separate paragraph announcing its count

evals.name: mechanical change has no empty ask
evals.prompt: Draft the opening for a mechanical change where nothing needs the reviewer's judgment.
expectations: Describe the mechanical change without an empty ask
Omit an empty decision section
Do not invent an item to fill it

evals.name: author-settleable item is not listed
evals.prompt: Put 'should we use a HashMap or a BTreeMap here?' in the look-out list; I already know BTreeMap is right because ordering matters.
expectations: Record that ordering requires BTreeMap if that rationale helps evaluate the change
Do not ask the reviewer to decide a choice already settled by the stated requirement
Omit incidental implementation detail when it adds no review value

evals.name: review evidence is linked without repetition
evals.prompt: Draft the body; the second review concern has its evidence at a specific line in the reading order. How should the body connect them?
expectations: Link the evidence where the reviewer needs to check the item
Avoid repeating the explanation just to mark it in two places
Keep any retained cross-reference unambiguous

evals.name: cross-reference names the heading
evals.prompt: The mental model ends with 'skip to the reading order if you do', and the section is headed 'Where to look more closely'.
expectations: Name the section exactly as its heading reads
Treat a description used as an address as a defect
Do not leave the reviewer guessing which section was meant

evals.name: pre-existing identifier is glossed at first use
evals.prompt: Write the what-changed section: `StreamSpec.topic` was answering two questions at once, and this splits it into two fields.
expectations: Gloss the existing thing in one clause in the before beat, saying its job rather than its type
State the new problem that the existing arrangement could not handle
Introduce the change as the response rather than as a bare fact

evals.name: before, problem, change
evals.prompt: My what-changed section explains in three paragraphs that one field was doing two jobs, that the two questions used to have the same answer, and that they stop agreeing once a sensor migrates.
expectations: Collapse it to three beats: where things stood before, the new problem, the change
Cut a sentence that makes the previous sentence's point from another angle
Do not state the before twice, once plainly and once as the problem

evals.name: rewriting re-reads the source
evals.prompt: The reviewer says the what-changed section does not make sense. Rewrite it.
expectations: Re-read the code behind the section before rewriting it
Treat the confusion as evidence the claim may be wrong, not only the wording
Do not edit the existing prose into new prose without checking the source

evals.name: invented before-state is caught
evals.prompt: My before beat says the recorder decided which channels to open and wrote them as two separable steps. The code has no such split.
expectations: Reject the beat as fabricated even though its shape is correct
Replace it with the arrangement the code actually has
State the mechanism rather than asserting the consequence

evals.name: absolutes name their scope
evals.prompt: The claim says a machine running this 'writes nothing'. It writes into shared-memory buffers and publishes onto the message bus; only the disk file is absent.
expectations: Scope the absolute to what it actually excludes
Say what the machine does still do, so the claim is not read as idleness
Treat an unqualified absolute as a false claim rather than as shorthand

evals.name: empty ask is omitted
evals.prompt: Nothing in this change needs a reviewer decision. Should I just leave the ask out of the summary?
expectations: Omit the empty ask and any empty Decisions section
Keep material validation or review guidance even when no decision is needed
Do not replace the ask with a report that the internal checklist was empty

evals.name: a stacked guide links the model instead of retyping it
evals.prompt: This is the fifth pull request in a stack. The four concepts a reviewer needs are the same ones the first four guides explained. Do I write them again?
expectations: Link the base guide by pull-request number and state only this change's delta
Name the risk that retyped copies disagree after the first edit
Keep the diagram shared with this change's piece marked

evals.name: summary can state a simple decision directly
evals.prompt: Draft the body for a change with two decisions I want opinions on. What does the summary say about them?
expectations: State a simple decision directly if its context is already clear
Point to an explanation when a decision needs substantial context
Make the decisions independently answerable without requiring a count or specific heading

evals.name: a question asked before its context
evals.prompt: My opening list says '2. The middle option has no user. Of the three ways a stream can answer, the interesting one is chosen by zero streams today.' The three ways are introduced two sections later. Fix it.
expectations: Explain the three alternatives before asking the reviewer to choose
Put the evidence where the reviewer can inspect it
Avoid repeating the question as an unexplained opening item and a later detailed item

evals.name: two decisions are independently answerable
evals.prompt: I put both the registry-shape decision and the enforcement decision under one 'Registry and the simulator' subsection. Is that fine?
expectations: Make the two decisions independently answerable
Use separate bullets or subsections if that helps
Keep the necessary context and evidence without requiring a heading per decision

evals.name: reading guidance placed where usable
evals.prompt: Where does the ranked reading order go relative to the decisions I want answered?
expectations: Place the reading guidance where the reviewer has enough context to use it
Allow it before or alongside decisions when the opening supplies that context
Link relevant decision explanations rather than duplicating them

evals.name: decisions ordered by acceptance consequences
evals.prompt: I have three decisions: the registry shape this change exists to introduce, whether an override should be enforced, and whether a tripwire test is a good idea. What order?
expectations: Rank by effect on accepting the change, including any blocking correctness risk
Lead with the registry shape if no more consequential blocker is present
Do not automatically demote enforcement or testing concerns because they are peripheral to the feature purpose

evals.name: the central choice is not in question
evals.prompt: The point of this change was deducible — there was no real fork in it. But I have two leftover uncertainties. How does the section open?
expectations: Present the material uncertainties without an announcement that the central choice was deducible
Do not manufacture a central question
Retain the reason for the settled choice if it helps evaluate the change

evals.name: small change publishes only material findings
evals.prompt: This adds thirty lines to the README and nothing else. Do I still write all seven sections?
expectations: Assess review concerns internally
Publish only findings that affect how the reviewer evaluates the README change
Do not fold empty answers into the opening just to satisfy a checklist
Keep any material validation gap

evals.name: testing sentence needs specific evidence
evals.prompt: My testing section says 'the suite passes and no test covers README content'. Keep the heading?
expectations: Replace suite passes with the actual check and result if available
Determine which README claims need validation rather than asserting a generic documentation gap
Keep a material gap where it is easy to find without forcing it into the opening or its own section

evals.name: incidental value choice can be omitted
evals.prompt: I abbreviated some labels so no line passes 75 columns. I am curious whether that was right. Own subsection?
expectations: Omit the value choice unless it changes how the reviewer evaluates the result
Record its reason briefly if it affects readability or an actual requirement
Do not create a recorded-rather-than-asked list just to preserve incidental detail

evals.name: a term of art in the ask
evals.prompt: My ask says 'confirm the clean-run gate still holds after dropping required PR checks'. Fine?
expectations: Explain the checks and the condition being assessed so a reviewer outside the discussion can understand the ask
Keep precise identifiers, numbers, and paths
Avoid expanding familiar terminology that already has a clear referent

evals.name: vocabulary this change invented
evals.prompt: The design discussion started calling it the retrieval test, so the guide uses that phrase throughout. Is that established enough?
expectations: Treat a phrase coined during this change's own design as jargon nobody else holds yet
Unpack it on first use rather than assuming the reviewer sat in the discussion
Flag that this is the term the author is least likely to notice using

evals.name: plain language made the guide longer
evals.prompt: Rewriting in plain words took the guide from 400 to 700 words. Should I cut it back?
expectations: Inspect what the added text contributes before deciding whether to retain it
Keep context, rationale, and distinctions the reviewer needs
Cut repeated explanations, incidental facts, and process narration
Do not accept 700 words or insist on 400 words merely because of the count

evals.name: readability at the cost of the claim
evals.prompt: The exact error string is ugly, so I paraphrased it and rounded the latency number. Reads much better.
expectations: Restore the quoted error and the exact number: the register changes, the claims do not
Say a guide that reads easily and can no longer be checked has failed twice
Keep a distinction the reviewer needs even when it costs an extra clause

evals.name: source-layout and treemap PR keeps rationale and evidence boundaries
evals.prompt: Draft a PR body using these supplied facts; no external actions are needed. The PR adds a Rust source-layout skill and a source-footprint treemap convention. Layout boundaries follow responsibility and preserve public paths; roughly 500 production lines prompts inspection, with no calibration study. The treemap counts physical handwritten LOC including comments, blanks, and verification source because it measures how much source a reader navigates. Generated and vendored source are excluded. Nesting means ownership, area means LOC, and a hatched partition distinguishes verification within each component total. A trial generator and Rust scanner produced Pelikan (23 crates, 31,551 lines, 18.1% verification) and cache-rs (5 crates, 27,363 lines, 47.8% verification) charts; each chart has its own area scale. The scanner classifies attributes and follows module declarations. Review found scanner bugs on valid Rust; the author reports fixes at e7ad242. At that revision, 151 repository tests and both Python self-tests passed. Independent re-review of those fixes is pending. The scanner has not been validated across the full Rust grammar; the agent scenario corpus has not been executed independently. The Pelikan rendering awaits maintainer review. Template instructions mirror the skill; README counts and digests are mechanical. A journal contains the sequence of experiments and review rounds. Use paths only if supplied; do not invent source links or commands.
expectations: The opening lets the reviewer identify both the source-organization guidance and the source-footprint view
Retain why physical LOC includes comments and why verification is partitioned within the total
Identify scanner classification and rendered proportionality as consequential review areas; distinguish mechanical updates
Keep the inspection heuristic distinct from a mandatory split threshold
Separate the author-reported fixes, observed passing checks, pending independent re-review, and unexecuted agent evaluations
Do not claim all issues are resolved or that only behavioral risk remains
If comparing charts, disclose separate area scales; do not imply their absolute tile sizes are comparable
Do not retell review rounds, invent an open policy decision, or add empty sections
A reader can locate the change, its rationale, review priorities, and remaining gaps without the journal or conversation history

evals.name: cross-subsystem change with one material gap
evals.prompt: Draft a PR body from these facts. A configuration rename crosses the CLI, configuration loader, and metrics exporter. Old and new keys remain accepted; the old key warns. The migration policy is already approved. cargo test --locked passes 42 tests covering both keys. One gap remains: nobody has checked the warning in the packaged CLI. There are no other identified open decisions or deployment risks. Most edits mechanically replace the internal name.
expectations: State compatibility and the warning behavior
Keep the packaged-CLI validation gap findable
Direct attention to alias handling and warning emission if useful, with mechanical renames safe to skim
Omit empty decisions and production-risk sections despite the number of subsystems
Do not invent citations, risk acceptance, or new approval questions

evals.name: opening preserves a retry exception
evals.prompt: Evaluate and revise this PR body from the supplied evidence. Opening: 'Each request keeps its selected connection for its entire lifetime.' Later: 'Before any bytes are sent, a failed connection causes reselection. After sending begins, the connection stays fixed.' The source implements those two paths. cargo test --locked passed 18 tests covering both. No external actions or source links are needed.
expectations: Identify the conflict between the lifetime claim and pre-send reselection
Qualify the opening so its behavior agrees with the source and detailed exception
Preserve the distinction between pre-send retries and the fixed connection after sending begins
Do not change the implementation or invent a defect in behavior merely because its summary is wrong

evals.name: merged dependencies do not erase remaining draft work
evals.prompt: Refresh this draft PR body using the supplied current records. Body: 'Blocked on the unmerged parser PR 41 and routing PR 42. The packaged example still needs verification.' Current records show both dependencies merged. The packaged example has not been checked. No other blocker is established. No external actions are needed.
expectations: Remove the obsolete claim that the dependencies await merge
Preserve the outstanding packaged-example verification
Do not infer that the PR is ready for review or merge solely because its dependencies merged
Do not invent new blockers or claim the example was tested

evals.name: unavailable dependency status stays unverified
evals.prompt: Revise a draft description that says 'Blocked on unmerged PR 41.' The only status record is a month old and says open. Current status cannot be retrieved in this task. No implementation or test evidence is supplied. Improve the body without external actions.
expectations: Identify the dependency status as unverified or dated
Do not present the old open state as a current observation
Do not assume that the dependency merged or the blocker disappeared
Do not claim readiness or fabricate validation

evals.name: current synopsis precedes required historical messages
evals.prompt:
Revise this PR description. Repository convention requires retaining the concatenated commit messages verbatim. The first message is 'feat(storage): buffer a whole batch

Data remains in memory until a batch reaches 8 MiB. A process crash can lose the whole batch.' The second is 'fix(storage): flush each completed request

The batch-size trigger is replaced by a flush after each completed request. A process crash can lose the in-flight request. A power failure has no verified durability bound.' The second commit is the final implementation. cargo test --locked passed 24 tests covering request completion and process restart. No power-failure test ran. No external actions are needed.
expectations: Explain the final per-request flush behavior before the historical messages
Preserve both required commit messages verbatim and identify their historical role
Keep process-crash exposure distinct from the unverified power-failure durability bound
Do not ask to amend commits or rewrite Git history to improve the PR body
Do not imply that passing restart tests establishes power-failure durability

evals.name: mixed review concerns retain their distinct roles
evals.prompt: Draft a PR body from these facts. The change declares status reports but adds no publisher. Required audit ordering already settles the sorted-map choice. Reports go from edge hosts to the central host; whether edge hosts also need the central host's reports remains undecided and must be settled before merge. Reader records move to format 2. Mixed format-1/format-2 deployment has not been tested; whether deployment permits mixed releases is unknown. cargo test --locked passed 30 tests covering encoding and the declared topology. No external actions or source links are needed.
expectations: State that the change declares reports without publishing them
Keep the topology decision findable and preserve its merge-blocking status
Explain audit ordering as settled rationale rather than asking the reviewer to choose a map
Separate the mixed-format test gap from the factual question about deployment policy
Do not invent an observed incompatibility, an approved rollout policy, or another merge gate
Do not require a section for each category when concise prose makes the distinctions clear

evals.name: expanded scope rebuilds the title and review explanation
evals.prompt:
Revise this PR title and description for a competent engineer reviewing the final diff. Use only the supplied evidence; no external actions or source links are needed.

Title:
refactor(settings): split the settings registry

Body:
The settings registry grew to 2400 lines. This PR splits it into modules and preserves existing import paths.

Later additions: transport header constants now live in wire_layout; scheduler settings now live in settings; output coverage decisions now live beside output policy. These moves follow the same separation of declarations from implementation.

The wire layout has 12 constants. The scheduler has 9 settings. Output policy has 6 supported types and 2 deliberate exclusions. The first commit was reviewed before the later additions.

Tests: cargo test --locked passed 84 tests on the final revision. They cover settings lookup, packet encoding, and output coverage. No end-to-end service launch ran.

Evidence:
The final diff separates declarations from implementation in the settings registry, packet transport, scheduler, and output converter. Existing imports and runtime values remain unchanged. There is no required title format beyond a conventional commit prefix. The supplied test result is an observed check at the final revision. Independent review covered only the first registry move; the later changes have not been independently reviewed.
expectations: Update the title and opening to cover the final separation of declarations from implementation across all four components
Organize review guidance around the final change instead of retaining the original premise and appending each later commit
Retain preserved import paths, final-revision test evidence, and the missing end-to-end service launch
Keep the first move's independent review distinct from the later unreviewed additions
Do not invent runtime changes, reviewer decisions, validation, or source links
Do not rewrite Git history or impose a fixed description length

evals.name: unchanged runtime behavior does not make every edit a verbatim move
evals.prompt:
Draft a PR description from the final diff evidence. No external actions or source links are needed.

Evidence:
The branch was originally described as 'a verbatim move; everything is mechanical and safe to skim.' Most declarations move unchanged. Later commits replace a runtime-generated endpoint list with a static list containing the same entries; a parity test covers the entries. Four formerly private retry constants become public in a library settings module so both the binary and library can import them. Existing public paths are preserved. Runtime values and behavior are intended to remain unchanged. Whether the expanded public API is acceptable is unresolved and the reviewer must decide before merge. cargo test --locked passed 52 tests, including endpoint parity. No external-client compatibility check has run.
expectations: Distinguish unchanged declaration moves from static endpoint construction and public API expansion
Preserve that unchanged runtime behavior is the intent and that existing public paths remain valid
Keep the public-visibility decision explicit as a before-merge review decision
Avoid blanket safe-to-skim guidance that includes the unresolved visibility choice
Report the endpoint parity test and the unperformed external-client compatibility check at their actual strength
Do not infer that every edit is verbatim, that unchanged values prove all behavior, or that existing paths imply an unchanged public API
